gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 'Apex + B300K' bundles on BLUETTI's own store cost $1 more than buying the same two items separately ($2,199 vs $2,198 for the Apex 200, $2,599 vs $2,598 for the Apex 300). It also doesn't state that the 'Lifting Power' figure on these power stations is not a motor-surge rating, so it can't be used to judge whether a sump pump will start.
standout_why: I compared against Consumer Reports' 'Best Sump Pump Backup Systems' page (cited, opened 2026-11-10) and ChatGPT's two answers. CR only says backup and combo units 'typically require a 12-volt deep-cycle marine battery, which is sold separately'. It tested with a 75 Ah marine battery and names no retailer, bundle, price or battery chemistry. ChatGPT gives an 'inverter + battery' range of $400–$1,500+. It names no power station and no expansion battery, and says nothing about surge versus lifting power or what a one-store cart costs. I did not open the uncited results (Ferguson, Pumpendium, Angi, ICLR, SSPMA). Amazon prices for the dedicated-pump kit could not be checked.
kit_items: Power station with UPS mode (keeps the existing AC primary pump running): BLUETTI Apex 300. BLUETTI's own sump-pump guide names it for whole-home protection. It has 2,764.8 Wh and 3,840 W output, and its lifting power (7,680 W, which is not a surge rating) is the only one in that guide above the top of its 1/2 HP surge range (4,100 W).
Expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K for Apex 300/200 (2,764.8 Wh LiFePO4). It doubles storage to 5,529.6 Wh. Buy it as a separate line item, because the Apex+B300K bundle costs $1 more.

Lower-cost alternative: BLUETTI Apex 200 (2,560 Wh, 3,200 W continuous, UPS rated ≤15 ms, enabled in the BLUETTI app). Its page lists no surge rating, only 5,400 W 'Lifting Power', so it fits a 1/3 HP pump more safely than a 1/2 HP one.

Dedicated battery backup pump (Amazon route): Wayne ESP25 plus Wayne's own WSB1275 75 Ah deep-cycle battery, which the ESP25 manual names. The battery is not included. Amazon prices could not be checked.

findings.label: UPS switchover time
findings.value: ≤15 ms; UPS mode must be enabled in the BLUETTI app
findings.note: The page warns that the transfer 'may not meet every device's requirements'.

findings.label: Rated AC output / published surge
findings.value: 3,200 W continuous; no surge rating listed, only 5,400 W 'Lifting Power'
findings.note: Lifting Power is BLUETTI's mode for resistive loads, not a motor-start rating. See the sump pump guide finding.

findings.label: Sump pump running and starting watts
findings.value: 1/3 HP: about 800 W running, 1,300–2,900 W surge. 1/2 HP: about 1,050 W running, 2,150–4,100 W surge. Size the inverter's surge rating to at least 1.5× the pump's starting watts.
findings.source_title: How Long Can a BLUETTI Portable Power Station Power a Sump Pump? (BLUETTI Team, 2026-10-05)
findings.note: These figures come from the maker's own blog. The same blog says the Elite 100 V2 is not recommended as a primary sump pump backup.

findings.label: Runtime on a 1/3 HP pump (BLUETTI's estimate)
findings.value: 11.0–16.6 h with the pump cycling 10–15 min per hour; about 2.1 h continuous on a 1/2 HP pump
findings.source_title: How Long Can a BLUETTI Portable Power Station Power a Sump Pump?
findings.note: BLUETTI's formula is Wh × 0.8 ÷ running W. My arithmetic with the B300K added (5,529.6 Wh): 5,529.6 × 0.8 ÷ 800 W = 5.5 h continuous on a 1/3 HP pump, or about 22–33 h at 10–15 min of running per hour.

findings.label: Battery for a backup pump (Consumer Reports)
findings.value: 12 V deep-cycle marine battery, sold separately; CR tested with 75 Ah
findings.source_title: Best Sump Pump Backup Systems - Consumer Reports
findings.note: No retailers, prices or bundles on the page.

findings.value: No: 'A battery (not included) must be installed to operate the back-up sump pump'
